full_judgment:
The opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Other Class Suit No. 398 of 1981 in the Second Court of Munsif, Jamalpur under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act for recovery of khas possession. The suit on transfer to the court of Munsif, Madarganj was renumbered there as Other Class Suit No. 81 of 1984. 

 9. The learned trial Judge held that the suit is maintainable in its present form. Learned trial Judge further held that the plaintiff filed the suit within prescribed period of time from the date of dispossession. The learned trial Judge further found that the suit is not bad for defect of parties. The learned trial Judge ultimately recorded the finding that the plaintiff through legal evidence could prove his possession and subsequent dispossession and he was entitled to get a decree of recovery of khas possession. With the above findings and deciding all the issues in favour of the plaintiff, the trial Judge decreed the suit. 

 The learned trial Judge, with the above decisions decreed the suit and granted the relief of recovery of khas possession. 

 27. Let me now turn to another aspect of the case. It is noticed that the plaintiff along with the relief of recovery of khas possession on the suit land also prayed for recording his name along with the names of the defendants in the record of right. The learned trial Judge refused to grant the said relief taking the view that granting of the said relief was beyond the scope in a suit under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act. The learned trial Judge is well founded on law in refusing to grant the said relief which is not at all permitted in a summary proceeding under section 9 of the Specific Relief Act.
